claims.text: HEA multilayers with coherent interfaces exhibit greater creep resistance than HEA multilayers with incoherent interfaces.
The initial material system consists of HEA multilayers having varying degrees of interface coherency.
Advanced microscopy techniques can manipulate interface coherency in HEA multilayers.
Advanced microscopy techniques can observe interface coherency in HEA multilayers.
Interface coherency influences the transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
The transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep affects overall creep resistance.
Coherent-interface HEA multilayers will have lower creep rates than incoherent-interface HEA multilayers under otherwise identical conditions.
A reduced creep rate in coherent-interface HEA multilayers indicates a transition toward dislocation-mediated creep.
The quantitative effect of interface coherency on HEA multilayer creep rates is unclear because empirical data are lacking.
